newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal new car sales up 8.2 percent yr/yr 1996.
newsitem.headline: Portugal new car sales up 8.2 percent yr/yr 1996.

text.p: Sales of new cars grew 8.2 percent to 217,913 units in Portugal in 1996, compared with 1995, the Association of Car Trade in Portugal (ACAP) said.
In December 1996, 20,151 new cars were sold, up 20.4 percent from December 1995.
"Unfortunately, the excessive burden of tax, notably the Car Tax (IA), continues to be an enormous constraint on the normal development of the car trade in our country," a statement said.

The average burden of tax on new car prices exceeded 50 percent in 1996, ACAP said. In an average case, if the basic cost of a car were, say, five million escudos, the general public would have to pay at least 7.5 million to buy the car.

"In the case of vehicles of 1,600 cc, the fiscal burden was about 70 percent, and in the case of cars of more than 2,000 cc, the level of tax often exceeded 100 percent of the new car price," ACAP said.
IA is levied in Portugal based on the cylinder capacity of vehicles.
Sales of four-wheel-drive vehicles rose 34.3 percent in 1996 to 10,003 units, while in December 1996 sales rose 56.8 percent year-on-year to 1,043.
ACAP said 74,446 light commercial vehicles were sold in Portugal in 1996, a 26.8 percent increase over 1995.

The most popular marque sold in Portugal in 1996 was Fiat with 32,187 units, 1.9 percent higher than in 1995, followed by Opel with 31,207 units, 2.1 percent down from 1995, and Renault with 27,550 units, up 6.9 percent.
